definition: A model trained to predict how much a human would prefer one output over another, used to provide a training signal for reinforcement learning from human feedback.
details: Reward models are typically trained on datasets of human comparisons between pairs of model outputs, and then used to score new outputs during the RL fine-tuning phase of alignment.
story: Picture a gambler who slowly learns which slot machines pay out, not by reading a manual but by pulling the lever. The machine is not handed the answers — it tries things, earns a reward or a miss, and slowly figures out what works. It learns the way a child learns to walk: wobble, fall, adjust, repeat. The learner writes its own textbook from consequences. That learn-by-reward loop is Reward Model.
